newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol steady, but EMU holds sway.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Notionnel vol steady, but EMU holds sway.

text.p: Implied volatility of French notionnel options traded on the MATIF was stagnant on Thursday, as jitters over EMU relaxed, traders said.

"People are generally not too worried, although there are still some scares in the market," said Jonathan Morris, a broker at Finacor in Paris. "People are still selling volatility in cash and listed options."

Traders said there was an air of calm, verging on cautious optimism, as EU Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said he believed Europe would be able to reach a deal over the proposed single European currency at a summit in Amsterdam next week. But a failure at that meeting could throw markets into turmoil, traders said.
Markets have been disorientated in the past few days, after France said it needed time to consider the stability pact before committing to it.

Implied volatility of July serial options was unchanged at 4.8 percent by 1015 GMT, while August was steady at 4.85 percent. September was little moved at 4.9 percent, and December was notionally at 5.9 percent, compared with 6.0 percent on Wednesday.
September notionnel futures were up six basis points at 128.02.

In July, front-month options, more than 2,800 lots of the 129.00 strike were traded. Also, a broker bought 500 lots of the 125.00 August puts, and 500 of the 124.00 puts, financing the deal by selling 500 of the 126.00 and 125.00 September puts.
"If he's got it wrong and the market rallies, this trade is still okay, as long as vol picks up before the end of July," said Morris.
A trader at a French brokerage said he would be a buyer of volatility at these levels, particularly as he said July volatility is near its cheapest level since it came on the board in April.
Although notionnel options were quiet, trade said they expected any concerns about EMU to manifest themselves initially at the short-end of the yield curve.
September PIBOR volatility was off at 26.0 percent, compared with 26.1 percent. The French trader said activity was steady, although it had calmed from the previous session.
On Wednesday, a French house bought 8,000 of the 96.00/95.70 September put spread and sold 8,000 of the 96.80 calls -- a so-called Rambo in France.
The trade would benefit from EMU-inspired turmoil, which would lead to selling of the September PIBOR future, sending volatility soaring.
September PIBOR futures were up three basis points at 96.45. -- Lisa Wilson, International Bonds Unit + 44 171 542 6137
